title: Ethiopian Physics University Entrance Exam 2018
description: Ethiopian Physics University Entrance Exam 2018 featuring 60 authentic questions with step-by-step solutions. Designed for Ethiopian national exam mastery.

questions.questionText: Pascal's principle states that a pressure added at the top of a liquid at rest in a cylindrical shape container
options: decreases the pressure at any point in the liquid by the same amount as that added at the top.
increases the pressure at any point in the liquid by a smaller amount than that added at the top.
increases the pressure at any point in the liquid by a greater amount than that added at the top.
increases the pressure at any point in the liquid by the same amount as that added at the top.
questions.explanation:
Pascal's principle states that when pressure is applied to an enclosed fluid, the pressure change is transmitted equally and undiminished throughout the fluid.

Therefore, if the pressure at the top is increased by a certain amount, the pressure at every other point in the fluid also increases by the same amount.

questions.questionText: A high-pressure system can be applied to
options: transport a fluid through a pipe.
generate cold water from steam or super-heated water.
reduce the gas in the bicycle and car tires.
biological sample to increase micro-organism activity.
questions.explanation:
A pressure difference causes a fluid to move from a region of higher pressure toward a region of lower pressure.

High-pressure systems can therefore be used to force liquids or gases through pipes and other channels.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following statements is correct about the characteristics of steady and turbulent fluid flow?
options: In each flow, fluid particles pass a given point in space with the same velocity.
In turbulent flow, the velocity of a fluid particles is the same at same point of a flow line in space unlike in the steady flow.
In steady flow, the adjacent layers of fluid do not cross each other unlike in the turbulent flow.
In each flow, the lines along which fluid particles move do not cross each other.
questions.explanation:
In steady or laminar flow, the fluid moves in smooth and orderly layers, and adjacent layers generally move without crossing one another.

Turbulent flow is irregular and contains eddies and mixing between different parts of the fluid.

questions.questionText: Our planet Earth has an orbital period of 365 days and its mean distance from the Sun is R_E = 1.495 × 10⁸ km. If there is another unknown planet whose mean distance from the Sun is R = 4R_E, how much is an orbital period of the unknown planet in terms of the days on the Earth?
options: 23360 days
2920 days
1460 days
730 days
questions.explanation:
Kepler's Third Law states that the square of the orbital period is proportional to the cube of the mean orbital radius, so T² ∝ R³.

Therefore, (T/T_E)² = (R/R_E)³ = 4³ = 64.

Taking the square root gives T/T_E = 8.

Since Earth's orbital period is 365 days, T = 8 × 365 = 2920 days.

questions.questionText:
A long current carrying wire is lying on the plane of this paper. The wire length is along the y-axis carrying current I along the positive y direction as shown in the figure below.

What is the direction of the magnetic field produced on the plane of the paper at indicated distance r from the wire along x-axis?
options: Towards the positive y direction at point a
Towards the negative x direction at point b
Perpendicular to the plane of the page at point b
Perpendicular to the plane of the page at point a
questions.explanation:
The magnetic field around a long straight current-carrying wire forms circular paths around the wire.

Using the right-hand rule, point your right thumb in the direction of the current, which is upward along the positive y-axis.

Your curled fingers show the direction of the magnetic field around the wire.

At point b, which is on the left side of the wire, the magnetic field points out of the page, so it is perpendicular to the plane of the paper.

questions.questionText:
Two identical vessels, A and B, are filled fully with two different liquids and opened to the atmosphere. When a student makes holes at the sides of the two vessels at equal height h from the bases of the vessels, she observes the water spilled out from A strikes the ground at a distance, x₁, and the water spilled out from vessel B strikes the ground at a distance x₂, as shown in the figure below.

If x₂ > x₁, which one of the following conclusions about the pressure and the fluids in the two vessels is correct?
options: The density of the liquid in vessel B is greater than that of the liquid in vessel A.
The absolute pressure at hole of vessel A is greater than that of at the hole of vessel B.
The liquid pressure at the hole of vessel B is less than that of at the hole of vessel A.
The atmospheric pressure on the liquid in vessel B is greater than that on vessel A.
questions.explanation:
The liquid leaving a hole has an exit speed that depends on the pressure difference between the liquid at the hole and the atmosphere.

For a liquid column, the gauge pressure is P = ρgh, where ρ is the liquid density and h is the depth of the hole below the liquid surface.

The holes are at the same height in identical vessels, so the liquid depth above each hole is the same.

Since x₂ > x₁, liquid B leaves with a greater speed and therefore has a greater pressure at the hole.

With the same liquid depth, this requires a greater density for liquid B.

questions.questionText: A unit vector is defined as
options: vector of magnitude zero, with arbitrary direction.
small vector in the direction of a given vector.
vector of magnitude one, with no unit.
vector of magnitude one, with specified unit.
questions.explanation:
A unit vector is a vector whose magnitude is exactly 1.

It has no physical unit and is mainly used to specify direction.

For example, î, ĵ, and k̂ are unit vectors along the x, y, and z axes respectively.

questions.questionText: Which of the following statements does NOT explain the importance of physics to society? Physics helps society by its direct contribution in
options: the development of cleaner energy sources.
the development of medical equipment.
developing strategies to combat climate change.
maintaining equality and justice in the society.
questions.explanation:
Physics contributes directly to society through areas such as energy production, medical technology, communication, transportation, and climate research.

Maintaining equality and justice is primarily related to law, ethics, politics, and social sciences rather than a direct application of physics.

questions.questionText: To form an image of a distant object, the refracting telescope uses
options: an objective convex lens to collect light and form an image which is magnified by the convex lens of the eyepiece.
convex mirror to collect light and forms an image which is magnified by the convex lens of the eyepiece.
an objective concave lens to collect light and forms an image which is magnified by the concave lens of the eyepiece.
convex mirror to collect light and forms an image which is magnified by the concave lens of the eyepiece.
questions.explanation:
A refracting telescope uses lenses rather than mirrors.

The objective is a convex lens with a long focal length and collects light from the distant object to form a real image.

The eyepiece is also a convex lens and acts as a magnifying glass to enlarge the image formed by the objective.

questions.questionText: Two plane mirrors inclined at an angle of 72° to each other. How many images are formed when an object is placed between them?
questions.explanation:
For two plane mirrors inclined at an angle θ, when 360°/θ is an integer, the number of images is n = 360°/θ - 1.

Here, θ = 72°, so 360°/72° = 5.

Therefore, n = 5 - 1 = 4 images.

questions.questionText: Given two vectors P⃗ = -5î + 3ĵ and Q⃗ = 2î + ĵ, what is the dot product of the vectors?
questions.explanation:
The dot product of two vectors is found by multiplying corresponding components and adding the results.

P⃗ · Q⃗ = (-5)(2) + (3)(1).

Therefore, P⃗ · Q⃗ = -10 + 3 = -7.

questions.questionText:
The displacement versus time graph of an object undergoing linear motion is shown in the figure below.

For the motion during the time interval between
options: t₂ and t₃, the velocity of the object is increasing and it is accelerating.
t₂ and t₃, the object is moving with a non-zero constant acceleration.
t₁ and t₂, the object is moving with a non-zero constant velocity.
0 and t₁, the velocity of the object is increasing and it is accelerating.
questions.explanation:
Velocity is represented by the slope of a displacement-time graph.

Between 0 and t₁, the slope of the curve continuously increases, meaning that the velocity is increasing.

An increasing velocity indicates that the object is accelerating.

questions.questionText: A nonconducting material that is inserted between the plates of a capacitor is known as
options: superconductor.
dielectric.
inductor.
semiconductor.
questions.explanation:
A dielectric is an insulating or nonconducting material placed between the plates of a capacitor.

It becomes polarized in an electric field and allows the capacitor to store more charge for the same potential difference.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following quantities is required to determine the specific heat capacity of a substance?
options: The volume of the substance
The boiling point of the substance
The mass of the substance
The density of the substance
questions.explanation:
Specific heat capacity is defined by the equation c = Q/(mΔT).

Here, Q is the heat supplied, m is the mass, and ΔT is the change in temperature.

Therefore, the mass of the substance is required when determining its specific heat capacity using this relationship.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following statements is correct about electric field lines?
options: Electric field lines of a charged body cross one another.
For a positively charged particle, the electric field lines point radially inward to the particle.
Electric field lines are parallel to the surface of the charged body.
The closer the electric field lines are, the stronger is the electric field.
questions.explanation:
The density of electric field lines represents the strength of the electric field.

Where field lines are closer together, the electric field is stronger.

Electric field lines do not cross, and for a positive charge they point outward rather than inward.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following statements is correct about critical and boiling points?
options: The critical point of a substance is constant, while its boiling point is dependent on the surrounding pressure.
The critical point is dependent both on temperature and pressure, while boiling point is independent of the surrounding pressure.
At the boiling point a single gaseous phase exists, while at the critical point both the liquid and gas phases coexist.
The boiling point of a substance is constant independent of pressure, while its critical point is dependent on the surrounding temperature.
questions.explanation:
The critical point is a characteristic point of a substance defined by a particular critical temperature and critical pressure.

Above the critical temperature, a gas cannot be liquefied simply by increasing pressure.

The boiling point, however, depends on the surrounding pressure and changes when the external pressure changes.

questions.questionText:
A circuit shown below consists of three resistors and two batteries.

The magnitude of current denoted by I₃ is
questions.explanation:
Kirchhoff's current law is first applied at the junction to relate the three branch currents.

Kirchhoff's voltage law is then applied around the two loops to obtain simultaneous equations for the unknown currents.

Using the polarity and circuit arrangement shown, solving these equations gives I₃ approximately equal to 0.45 A.

questions.questionText: A 25.0 liter container made of copper is completely filled with glycerin at a temperature of 20 °C. The coefficient of linear expansion of copper is α = 1.7 x 10⁻⁵ °C⁻¹ and that of volume expansion of glycerin is γ = 4.8 x 10⁻⁴ °C⁻¹. If the system is heated to a temperature of 80 °C, what volume of glycerin will overflow from the container?
options: 1.085 liter
0.868 liter
0.804 liter
0.651 liter
questions.explanation:
The temperature change is ΔT = 80 - 20 = 60 °C.

The volume expansion coefficient of copper is approximately γ_cu = 
3α = 3(1.7 × 10⁻⁵) = 5.1 × 10⁻⁵ °C⁻¹.

The apparent expansion coefficient is γ_app = γ_glycerin - γ_cu = 
4.8 × 10⁻⁴ - 5.1 × 10⁻⁵ =
 4.29 × 10⁻⁴ °C⁻¹.

The overflow volume is V = V₀γ_appΔT = 
25.0 × 4.29 × 10⁻⁴ × 60 ≈ 0.644 L.

questions.questionText: For a coil placed in a variable magnetic field, Lenz's law states that the direction of the induced current in the coil is in such a way as to
options: make the flux through the coil zero.
oppose the flux change through the coil.
decrease the flux through the coil.
increase the flux through the coil.
questions.explanation:
Lenz's law states that the induced current flows in a direction that opposes the change in magnetic flux responsible for producing the current.

It does not necessarily oppose the magnetic flux itself; it opposes the change in flux.

Therefore, option 1 is correct.

questions.questionText: Considering the concentration of dopants in different section of a transistors, which one of the following describes a correct order from lowest to highest?
options: Emitter, Base, Collector
Collector, Base, Emitter
Base, Emitter, Collector
Base, Collector, Emitter
questions.explanation:
In a bipolar junction transistor, the base is lightly doped, the collector is moderately doped, and the emitter is heavily doped.

Therefore, the dopant concentration increases in the order Base, Collector, Emitter.

questions.questionText: If the magnitude of magnetic field produced at a distance of 2 cm from a long straight current carrying wire is 1.2 T, then what is the magnitude of magnetic field at a distance of 3 cm from the wire?
questions.explanation:
The magnetic field around a long straight current-carrying wire is inversely proportional to the distance from the wire, so B ∝ 1/r.

Therefore, B₂ = B₁(r₁/r₂).

Substituting the values gives B₂ = 1.2 × (2/3) = 0.8 T.

questions.questionText: Which of the following circuit diagrams correctly represents a transistor-configurations that is used to get both current and voltage gain?
options: Common Collector configuration (Input at Base/Collector, Output at Emitter)
Common Emitter configuration (Input at Base, Output at Collector, Emitter common)
Common Base configuration (Input at Emitter, Output at Collector, Base common)
Common Collector configuration (Input at Base, Output at Emitter)
questions.explanation:
The common-emitter configuration can provide both significant current gain and voltage gain.

As a result, it can provide substantial power amplification and is widely used in amplifier circuits.

The input is applied between the base and emitter, while the output is taken from the collector circuit.

questions.questionText: Among the following analog circuits, consisting of two switches A and B, a lamp Y, and voltage source, which one functions as a NAND gate?
options: Parallel switches in series with lamp Y (OR gate)
Series switches in series with lamp Y (AND gate)
Series switches A and B connected in parallel across lamp Y
Parallel switches A and B connected in parallel across lamp Y (NOR gate)
questions.explanation:
A NAND gate produces a LOW output only when both inputs are HIGH.

In the given circuit, when both switches A and B are closed, the parallel path bypasses the lamp, causing the lamp to turn off.

For all other combinations, the lamp remains on.

Thus, the circuit behaves according to the NAND truth table.

questions.questionText: Suppose a 50 Hz outlet voltage of 10,000 V needs to be reduced to 220 V using a stepdown transformer. How many turns does the primary coil on the transformer have if the secondary coil has 110 turns?
questions.explanation:
For an ideal transformer, the voltage ratio equals the turns ratio: Vₚ/Vₛ = Nₚ/Nₛ.

Substituting the values gives 10,000/220 = Nₚ/110.

Therefore, Nₚ = (10,000 × 110)/220 = 5000 turns.

questions.questionText: During collision between two objects, the impulse imparted on each object is equal to the
options: net force acting on the object divided by the time for collision.
change in momentum of the object.
product of change in momentum and time for collision.
change of momentum of the object divided by the time for collision.
questions.explanation:
Impulse is defined as the product of force and the time interval over which the force acts.

According to the impulse-momentum theorem, impulse is equal to the change in momentum.

Therefore, J = Δp.

questions.questionText: In an automobile that contains engine and fuel, chemical energy of the fuel is partially converted to kinetic energy of the automobile and partially to thermal energy. In this process, the
options: energy of the automobile is not conserved because it does not exist persistently in chemical form.
kinetic energy of the automobile is considered as a created energy because it appears in a new form.
amount of energy converted to thermal energy is considered as destroyed because it decreases the efficiency of the automobile.
energy of the automobile is conserved because it is not destroyed but converted to kinetic and thermal energies.
questions.explanation:
The law of conservation of energy states that energy cannot be created or destroyed.

It can only be transformed from one form into another.

In an automobile, chemical energy stored in the fuel is transformed into kinetic energy, thermal energy, and other forms.

Therefore, the total energy is conserved even though not all of it becomes useful kinetic energy.

questions.questionText: A uniform disk of radius 10.0 cm is rotating at an angular velocity of 20.0 rad/s about an axis through its center. What is the centripetal acceleration of a point at a distance of 6.0 cm from the axis?
options: 2.0 m/s²
1.2 m/s²
questions.explanation:
The centripetal acceleration of a point in circular motion is given by a_c = ω²r.

The distance from the axis is 6.0 cm = 0.06 m.

Substituting ω = 20.0 rad/s and r = 0.06 m gives a_c = (20.0)²(0.06) = 24.0 m/s².

Therefore, option 0 is correct.

questions.questionText: A block of mass 20.0 kg is placed on a horizontal surface. If the coefficient of kinetic friction between the block and the surface is 0.25, what horizontal force must be applied on the block to accelerate it uniformly with 3.0 m/s²?
questions.explanation:
The kinetic friction force is f_k = μ_kmg.

Using g = 10 m/s², f_k = 0.25 × 20 × 10 = 50 N.

The net force required to produce the acceleration is ma = 20 × 3 = 60 N.

Therefore, the applied force must overcome friction and provide the net force: F = 50 + 60 = 110 N.

questions.questionText: A 0.3 kg ball moving with a velocity of 0.9 m/s along the positive x-axis collides with a 0.2 kg ball moving with a velocity of 1.2 m/s along the negative x-axis. What is the velocity of the center of mass of the two balls before collision?
options: 1.02 m/s along the negative x-axis
0.06 m/s along the negative x-axis
1.02 m/s along the positive x-axis
0.06 m/s along the positive x-axis
questions.explanation:
The velocity of the center of mass is v_cm = (m₁v₁ + m₂v₂)/(m₁ + m₂).

Taking the positive x-direction as positive, v₁ = +0.9 m/s and v₂ = -1.2 m/s.

Therefore, v_cm = [(0.3)(0.9) + (0.2)(-1.2)]/(0.3 + 0.2).

This gives v_cm = (0.27 - 0.24)/0.5 = 0.06 m/s.

The positive sign means the center of mass moves along the positive x-axis.

questions.questionText: What amount of heat energy is required to raise the temperature of 0.15 kg of silver from 20 °C to 100 °C? (Specific heat capacity of silver is 233.0 J/kg·°C)
questions.explanation:
The heat required to change the temperature of a substance is Q = mcΔT.

The temperature change is ΔT = 100 - 20 = 80 °C.

Therefore, Q = 0.15 × 233.0 × 80 = 2796 J.

Hence, option 2 is correct.

questions.questionText: The second condition of equilibrium states that the sum of all
options: torques acting on an object must be zero.
torques acting on an object must be non-zero constant.
forces acting on an object must be non-zero constant.
forces acting on an object must be zero.
questions.explanation:
For a rigid body to be in rotational equilibrium, the net torque about any point must be zero.

This condition is written as ∑τ = 0.

The first condition of equilibrium concerns the net force, while the second condition concerns the net torque.

questions.questionText: During a charging process by induction, a positively charged rod is brought closed to a neutral metal sphere mounted on an insulated stand without touching it. Then, the metal sphere
options: gains some protons whenever it is grounded.
gains some electrons, whenever it is grounded.
loses some electrons, whenever it is grounded.
becomes positively charged, whenever it is grounded.
questions.explanation:
A positively charged rod attracts free electrons toward the nearby side of the neutral metal sphere.

When the sphere is grounded, electrons can flow from the Earth into the sphere because they are attracted by the positive rod.

Thus, the sphere gains electrons and becomes negatively charged after the grounding and separation process.

questions.questionText: A positively charged rod is brought near to a neutral electroscope A and a negatively charged rod is brought near to a neutral electroscope B. What will happen to the gold foils of the electroscopes? The gold foils of
options: electroscope A attract and that of B repels each other.
electroscope A repels and that of B attracts each other.
both electroscopes repel each other.
both electroscopes attract each other.
questions.explanation:
When a charged rod is brought near a neutral electroscope, charges inside the electroscope redistribute by electrostatic induction.

For the positively charged rod, electrons are attracted toward the upper part, leaving the gold leaves with positive charge.

For the negatively charged rod, electrons are repelled toward the leaves, making both leaves negatively charged.

In both electroscopes, the two leaves acquire charges of the same sign and therefore repel each other.

questions.questionText: A particle moving with a speed of v₀ to the right starts accelerating uniformly with acceleration a. The total distance covered by the particle during the time interval t is s. Assuming the right direction is positive, which one of the following equations enables us to calculate the time t in terms v₀, a and s?
options: t = (v₀ - √(v₀² + 2as)) / 2a
t = (v₀ + √(v₀² + 2as)) / a
t = (-v₀ + √(v₀² + 2as)) / 2a
t = (-v₀ + √(v₀² + 2as)) / a
questions.explanation:
For uniformly accelerated motion, displacement is given by s = v₀t + ½at².

Rearranging gives at² + 2v₀t - 2s = 0.

Using the quadratic formula gives t = (-v₀ ± √(v₀² + 2as))/a.

Since time must be positive, the positive root is selected.

Therefore, t = (-v₀ + √(v₀² + 2as))/a.

questions.questionText: A weight of 1000 N suspended from an aluminum wire of length 2.5 m causes a 4.0 x 10⁻³ tensile strain on the wire. What is the change in length of the aluminum wire?
options: 1 cm
0.1 cm
10 cm
questions.explanation:
Tensile strain is defined as strain = ΔL/L₀.

Therefore, the change in length is ΔL = strain × L₀.

Substituting the values gives ΔL = (4.0 × 10⁻³)(2.5) = 0.010 m.

Since 0.010 m = 1 cm, the change in length is 1 cm.

questions.questionText: The acceleration of an object is defined as the time rate of change in
options: position of the object.
velocity of the object.
displacement of the object.
distance travelled by the object.
questions.explanation:
Acceleration is the rate at which velocity changes with time.

It is expressed mathematically as a = Δv/Δt for average acceleration or a = dv/dt for instantaneous acceleration.

Therefore, acceleration is the time rate of change of velocity.

questions.questionText:
The figure shown below represents the position-time graph of uniformly accelerated ball in a straight line.

The instantaneous velocity of the ball at point x is equal to
options: the slope of the tangent line at point x.
the total distance travelled to the total time, t₃ - t₁.
the ratio of the position at x (s₂) to the time t₂.
the average velocity during the time interval between t₁ and t₃.
questions.explanation:
Instantaneous velocity is the velocity of an object at a particular instant of time.

On a position-time graph, instantaneous velocity is equal to the slope of the tangent at the point representing that instant.

Therefore, at point x, the instantaneous velocity is the slope of the tangent line at x.

questions.questionText: The efficiency of a simple machine is defined as the ratio between
options: work output and mechanical advantage.
work output and velocity ratio.
mechanical advantage and velocity ratio.
work input and velocity ratio.
questions.explanation:
The efficiency of a simple machine is the ratio of useful work output to work input.

It can also be expressed in terms of mechanical advantage and velocity ratio as η = MA/VR.

Therefore, the efficiency is the ratio of mechanical advantage to velocity ratio.

questions.questionText: Static friction force is different from kinetic friction force in that, it
options: is a friction force between two objects that are at rest relative to each other.
has a maximum value which is often lower than the kinetic friction.
is a friction force between two objects that are moving relative to each other.
has higher value in smooth surfaces than in rough surfaces.
questions.explanation:
Static friction acts between two surfaces that are at rest relative to each other and prevents the surfaces from beginning to slide.

Its magnitude adjusts to oppose the applied force up to a maximum value.

Kinetic friction acts when the surfaces are already sliding relative to each other.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following statements is correct about simple machines?
options: machine can be designed to be a force multiplier, a speed multiplier, and a direction changer at the same time.
When a machine is designed so that its velocity ratio is greater than 1, it is called a speed multiplier.
machine which is designed so that its mechanical advantage is less than 1 is called a force multiplier.
When a machine is designed so that its velocity ratio is less than 1 is called a speed multiplier.
questions.explanation:
A speed multiplier increases the speed or distance moved by the load compared with the effort.

For a machine acting as a speed multiplier, the velocity ratio is less than 1.

Therefore, when VR < 1, the machine is classified as a speed multiplier.

questions.questionText:
The velocity-time graph of a moving object along a straight line is shown in the figure below.

What is the total displacement of the object during the total period of motion?
options: 8 m
questions.explanation:
Displacement is equal to the signed area under a velocity-time graph.

From 0 to 8 s, the positive area is the area of the trapezoid: ½(8 + 4)(2) = 12 m.

From 8 to 10 s, the velocity is negative, so the triangular area is -½(2)(2) = -2 m.

From 10 to 12 s, the velocity is zero, so the displacement is 0 m.

Therefore, total displacement = 12 - 2 = 10 m.

questions.questionText: A forklift truck applied a force of F⃗ = 30 N, East on an object and dragged it through a distance of 200 m along a horizontal frictionless surface in a time of 5 minutes. The average power output of the truck is
questions.explanation:
Work done is W = Fd because the force and displacement are in the same direction.

Therefore, W = 30 × 200 = 6000 J.

The time is 5 minutes = 5 × 60 = 300 s.

Average power is P = W/t = 6000/300 = 20 W.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following statements is correct about the property of magnetic field lines?
options: Outside a bar magnets, magnetic field lines emerge from the south pole and enter to the north pole.
Magnetic field lines cross each other.
Magnetic field lines form closed loops.
Magnetic field lines are closer to each other in a region where the magnetic field is weaker.
questions.explanation:
Magnetic field lines always form continuous closed loops.

Outside a bar magnet, they travel from the north pole toward the south pole, while inside the magnet they return from south to north.

Magnetic field lines do not cross one another because crossing would imply two different field directions at the same point.

questions.questionText:
Three resistors R₁, R₂, and R₃ are connected first in series and then in parallel with identical voltage source (vₛ). The potential differences across the resistors are measured with voltmeters and represented by v₁, v₂, ..., v₆ as shown in the figure below.

Which one of the following relations is correct about the potential differences across the resistors and the applied voltage source?
options: v₄ = v₅ = v₆ = vₛ
v₄ + v₅ + v₆ = vₛ
v₁ + v₂ + v₃ = v₄ + v₅ + v₆
v₁ = v₂ = v₃ = vₛ
questions.explanation:
In a parallel circuit, each resistor is connected directly across the same two terminals of the voltage source.

Therefore, the potential difference across each resistor is equal to the source voltage.

Thus, v₄ = v₅ = v₆ = vₛ.

questions.questionText: Two equal point charges of +3.6 x 10⁻⁶ C are placed 1.0 cm apart to each other. What is the magnitude of the electrostatic force between the charges?
questions.explanation:
Coulomb's law gives the electrostatic force as F = k|q₁q₂|/r².

The distance must be converted from 1.0 cm to 0.01 m.

Substituting k = 8.99 × 10⁹ N·m²/C² and q₁ = q₂ = 3.6 × 10⁻⁶ C gives F ≈ 1165 N.

This is approximately 1170 N.

questions.questionText:
Suppose the figure shown below represents some portion of the electromagnetic spectrum.

Which one of the following is correct about the nature of the electromagnetic waves represented by X and Y?
options: Waves X have longer wavelength than waves Y.
Waves Y have higher speed than waves X.
Waves X and Y has the same frequency.
Waves X have higher frequency than waves Y.
questions.explanation:
The electromagnetic spectrum is arranged from longer wavelength and lower frequency to shorter wavelength and higher frequency.

Since X is located before infrared, it represents electromagnetic waves with longer wavelengths than the waves represented by Y, which is beyond ultraviolet.

All electromagnetic waves travel at the same speed in vacuum, so Y does not have a higher speed than X.

questions.questionText: A light ray passing from air to glass has an angle of incidence 37° with the normal. If the refractive index of the glass is 1.54, what is the angle of refraction of the light?
options: θ = sin⁻¹ (1.0)
questions.explanation:
Snell's law states that n₁sinθ₁ = n₂sinθ₂.

For air, n₁ ≈ 1, while for glass n₂ = 1.54 and θ₁ = 37°.

Therefore, sinθ₂ = sin37°/1.54 ≈ 0.6018/1.54 ≈ 0.39.

Thus, θ₂ = sin⁻¹(0.39).

questions.questionText:
An electron moving at speed of 5.0 × 10⁷ m/s along the positive x-axis enters a uniform magnetic field of 1.5 T directed along the negative y-axis as shown in the figure below.

What is the magnetic force exerted on the electron at the moment it enters into the uniform magnetic field?
options: 8.0 x 10⁻¹² N, directed out of the page
1.2 x 10⁻¹¹ N, directed in to the page
1.2 x 10⁻¹¹ N, directed out of the page
8.0 x 10⁻¹² N, directed in to the page
questions.explanation:
The magnitude of the magnetic force is F = |q|vBsinθ.

The velocity and magnetic field are perpendicular, so θ = 90° and sin90° = 1.

Therefore, F = (1.6 × 10⁻¹⁹)(5.0 × 10⁷)(1.5) = 1.2 × 10⁻¹¹ N.

Using the right-hand rule for a positive charge, v⃗ × B⃗ points out of the page.

Because an electron is negatively charged, the force direction is opposite, so it points into the page.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following statements correctly defines the characteristic feature of a mechanical waves?
options: The number of complete waves passing a given point per second is called time period.
The distance between two adjacent peaks of the wave is called amplitude.
The distance that the wave travels in one second is called frequency.
The minimum distance between two identical points on adjacent waves is called wavelength.
questions.explanation:
Wavelength is the shortest distance between two consecutive points on a wave that are in the same phase.

For example, the distance from one crest to the next crest or from one trough to the next trough is one wavelength.

questions.questionText: The speed of sound is greatest in which one of the following materials?
options: Water
Copper
Oil
Air
questions.explanation:
Sound generally travels fastest through solids because their particles are closely packed and strongly connected.

Among the materials listed, copper is a solid, while water and oil are liquids and air is a gas.

Therefore, sound travels fastest in copper.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following statements is correct about graphical and algebraical representation of a vector? Vector is represented
options: graphically by an arrow in which the length of the arrow represents the magnitude of the vector to the appropriate chosen scale.
graphically by an arrow in which the length of the arrow is equal to the magnitude of the vector.
algebraically by a segment line in which the length of the segment line represents the magnitude of the vector.
graphically by a bold letter A or with an arrow over the letter like A⃗.
questions.explanation:
A vector is represented graphically by a directed arrow.

The direction of the arrow represents the direction of the vector, while its length represents the magnitude according to a chosen scale.

The actual arrow length does not necessarily equal the numerical magnitude unless the scale is one unit of length per unit of magnitude.

questions.questionText:
A simple first-class lever machine is used to lift a load of 500 N by applying an effort of 300 N, as shown in the diagram below.

What is the velocity ratio of the machine?
questions.explanation:
For a lever, the velocity ratio is the distance moved by the effort divided by the distance moved by the load.

For a first-class lever, this is equal to the effort arm divided by the load arm.

Therefore, VR = 5/2 = 2.50.

questions.questionText: A car moves at speed of 80.0 km/hr for 1.0 hour to East then back to West in which it travels at speed of 60.0 km/hr for 2.0 hrs. What is the average velocity of the car during its motion?
options: 66.7 km/hr, West
13.3 km/hr, West
66.7 km/hr, East
13.3 km/hr, East
questions.explanation:
Average velocity is total displacement divided by total time, not total distance divided by total time.

The eastward displacement is 80 km, while the westward displacement is 60 × 2 = 120 km.

Taking east as positive, total displacement = 80 - 120 = -40 km, meaning 40 km west.

Total time = 1 + 2 = 3 hours.

Average velocity = -40/3 ≈ -13.3 km/hr.

questions.questionText:
Three velocity vectors that are drawn by the scale of 1 cm to a velocity of 10 m/s is shown in figure below.

What is the resultant velocity of the three velocity vectors?
options: 20√2 m/s at 45° from the positive x-axis
10√41 m/s at 45° from the positive x-axis
10 m/s to the negative y-axis
50 m/s to the negative y-axis
questions.explanation:
Add the x-components and y-components of the three velocity vectors separately.

The x-components are -2 cm, +2 cm, and 0 cm, giving a resultant x-component of 0 cm.

The y-components are 0 cm, -1.5 cm, and -3.5 cm according to the figure, giving a resultant y-component of -5 cm.

Using the scale 1 cm = 10 m/s, the resultant magnitude is 5 × 10 = 50 m/s.

Since the x-component is zero and the y-component is negative, the direction is along the negative y-axis.

questions.questionText: Radioactivity is defined as
options: the spontaneous disintegration of unstable nuclei to form more stable nuclei.
phenomenon where by a single heavy nucleus is assembled from two or more lighter nuclei.
the spontaneous emission of electromagnetic radiation from a heavy nucleus.
the disintegration of a heavy nuclei into two lighter nuclei when bombarded by a neutron.
questions.explanation:
Radioactivity is the spontaneous process in which an unstable atomic nucleus changes into a more stable nucleus by emitting radiation.

The emitted radiation may consist of alpha particles, beta particles, or gamma rays.

Therefore, the most complete definition is the spontaneous disintegration of unstable nuclei to form more stable nuclei.

questions.questionText: The difference between conventional X-ray and CT-scan is that in the case of X-ray the machine that sends X-rays through the patient's body is
options: stationary, whereas in CT-scan a rotating X-ray machine is used.
rotating in the opposite direction of the detector which are stationary in the case of CT-scan.
rotating, whereas in CT-scan a stationary X-ray machine is used.
stationary but the patient is moving, unlike in case of CT scan.
questions.explanation:
In conventional X-ray imaging, the X-ray source remains essentially stationary and produces a two-dimensional projection image.

In a CT scan, the X-ray source and detectors rotate around the patient to collect many projections from different angles.

These measurements are then used to construct cross-sectional images.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following statements appropriately describes the application of physics knowledge in defense technology?
options: Radar is used for military purposes to detect a distant object by using sound waves signal.
Infrared devices are used by the military for purposes like night vision, navigation, hunting, and detecting hidden-objects.
Infrared devices are used in the military to magnify objects that can be seen with ordinary light.
Radar is used for military purposes like controlling air traffic, observation of weather, and navigation of ships.
questions.explanation:
Infrared radiation is associated with thermal energy emitted by objects.

Infrared devices can detect heat differences and can therefore be used for night vision, tracking, navigation, and detecting objects that are difficult to see with ordinary visible light.

Radar, on the other hand, uses radio waves rather than sound waves.

questions.questionText: A force F acts on an object of mass m and produces an angular displacement Δθ, and angular acceleration α in a time interval Δt. If the moment of inertia of the object about the axis of rotation is I, the magnitude of torque τ on the object is expressed as
options: τ = I / α
τ = m α
τ = I α
τ = F α
questions.explanation:
The rotational form of Newton's second law relates net torque to moment of inertia and angular acceleration.

The relationship is τ = Iα.

Here, τ is torque, I is moment of inertia, and α is angular acceleration.

questions.questionText: What is the binding energy of the nucleus of helium ⁴₂He? (Mass of ⁴₂He = 4.002603 u, mₚ = 1.007900 u, mₙ = 1.008665 u, 1 amu = 931.1 MeV)
questions.explanation:
A helium-4 nucleus contains two protons and two neutrons.

The total mass of the separate nucleons is 2(1.007900) + 2(1.008665) = 4.033130 u.

The mass defect is Δm = 4.033130 - 4.002603 = 0.030527 u.

Using E = Δmc² and 1 u = 931.1 MeV, the binding energy is E = 0.030527 × 931.1 ≈ 28.424 MeV.

questions.questionText: A horizontal distance jumper athlete jumps from the ground with initial speed v at an angle θ with the horizontal. For the constant initial speed, the range R is related to the maximum height h as
options: R = 4h if θ = 45°
R = 3h if θ = 37°
questions.explanation:
For a projectile launched and landing at the same level, the range is R = v²sin2θ/g.

The maximum height is h = v²sin²θ/(2g).

Dividing the range by the maximum height gives R/h = 4cotθ.

For θ = 45°, cot45° = 1, so R = 4h.
